title: How do we compare a family's heights?
description: A group project compares a student with a sample family's mean height and then looks at one-minute and three-minute time guesses. The mean, median and range are found for the sample data and checked.
teaching_notes: One idea: a mean shows a typical value for a group, and each member can be compared with it. Watch for children who compare a student with a single family member instead of the family mean.

video_script.why: The child can find a mean and a median and now pools data from a group and compares each person with a mean.
video_script.substitution: A sample family and four sample time guesses stand in for the group's real data.
video_script.anchor: Sample data. Family heights in cm: 172, 160, 148, 135. One-minute guesses in seconds: 52, 61, 48, 66. Three-minute guesses in seconds: 150, 195, 170, 210.
video_script.payoff_line: For the samples, the family mean is one hundred and fifty three point seven five centimetres.

final_answer.value: For the samples: family mean 153.75 cm, median 154 cm; mean estimates 56.75 s for 1 minute and 181.25 s for 3 minutes; repeat with your group's data
final_answer.spoken: for the samples, the family mean is one hundred and fifty three point seven five centimetres

maths_rules: sample family heights 172, 160, 148, 135 cm: total 615, mean 615 ÷ 4 = 153.75 cm
a student of 148 cm beside the family mean 153.75 cm: 153.75 - 148 = 5.75 cm shorter
video_script.design: A student bar beside a family mean bar, then two small dot plots of time guesses, each with its mean marked.
open_questions: The book gives two projects to a group, so the family heights and the time guesses are sample data from the worklist, labelled sample on screen. Both projects are covered once with the same steps.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, describe the family. The four heights add up to six hundred and fifteen centimetres.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Six hundred and fifteen divided by four is one hundred and fifty three point seven five.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Sort the heights. The median is halfway between the middle two, one hundred and forty eight and one hundred and sixty. That is one hundred and fifty four.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>The range is thirty seven, from one hundred and thirty five to one hundred and seventy two.
